picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 29, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. away.headline: Arizona football: CB Jay’Vion Cole to miss Texas Tech game, 2 injured receivers could return
away.blurb: CB Jay’Vion Cole is listed as out on the first availability report issued by the Big 12 Conference, one of four players ruled out for the matchup with the 13th-ranked Red Raiders.. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. Both are seeking another emergency injunction to restore their eligibility after each appeared in a few games earlier this season. For Texas Tech, running back Cameron Dickey is listed as questionable. He’s missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Arizona could get back a pair of injured wide receivers for Saturday’s Top 25 showdown at Texas Tech, but it will also be without its lockdown corner Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner.

away.headline: WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out
away.blurb: WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The first SEC availability report of Auburn week is out, and No. 12 Ole Miss has two key starters listed as questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis are both questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Running back Kewan Lacy is out, as expected, after dislocating his shoulder in last week's loss at Texas. Jalyn Crawford questionable after big night at Texas Pete Golding said Monday that Crawford “played his best game” at Texas and is “starting to show who we thought he was.” Losing him would be a big blow to a secondary that is already thin. Safety Edwin Joseph is out again as he works his way back from a procedure, and Golding said Monday he did not “feel great” about Joseph's chances this week. Safety MJ Preston, cornerback Cedrick Beavers, cornerback Iverson McCoy and safety Nascar McCoy are also out. Terez Davis questionable, but trending up Davis missed the Texas game after being a game-time decision, and he is questionable again to start the week. But Golding sounded confident Monday that his left tackle will be back. “Probably could have done it, but we didn't know what it was going to look like after and could have made it worse,” Golding said of holding Davis out in Austin. “So that's one definitely that we feel like, throughout this week, that we'll get back for this weekend.” Without Davis, Connor Howes moved to left tackle and Tommy Kinsler started at right tackle, and the line did not allow a sack. Howes and center Brycen Sanders are both listed as probable. Kewan Lacy out, Makhi Frazier steps in Ole Miss will also be without wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr., linebacker Ant Davis Jr. and offensive lineman Emanuel Faulkner. Defensive tackle Michai Boireau is probable. Auburn's list is short. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are out, and wide receiver Jeremiah Koger is questionable. The SEC releases availability reports on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday evenings of game week, with a final update on game day. The Thursday report comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT, and the final report is due about 90 minutes before Saturday's 11:45 a.m. kickoff. away.headline: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gives key injury update on Tai Buster
away.blurb: Sophomore Tai Buster was expected to be a key piece of Auburn's offensive line rotation this season, but a preseason setback has kept him away from the field . This week, Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gave a positive report for Buster's availability, saying he could be available to play as early as a few weeks. “Tai (Buster) has worked his tail off. I give Tai a lot of credit. He is working through return to play," Golesh said Monday. "The hope is that here in a couple of weeks, we get him fully integrated in practice, and it gives us a chance to see where he is." For injured players, it can take days or weeks to catch up and return to their routine, but Golesh says that will not be the case for Buster. Buster has remained immersed in practice and should return to full speed quickly. "He’s been engaged; I give him a lot of credit again, he’s been engaged," Golesh said. "He’s itching to get back out there. I thought when he got banged up, he was competing at a high level. We’re excited to get him back here soon.” Adding Buster to the rotation will not solve every issue the offensive line faces, but having an extra body will help keep linemen, especially at guard, fresh during Auburn's final stretch of regular-season games. The Tigers will be without Buster for their next game, Saturday at Ole Miss, but he could return in November to assist Auburn with their pursuit of bowl eligibility. The offensive line has been a weak spot for the Auburn Tigers this season, mostly due to a lack of depth. Three of Auburn's typical starters have logged over 400 snaps this season. Two others have played at least 300 snaps. Jacob Strand and Kenneth McManus have logged adequate snaps at multiple positions across the line this season. picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odd have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). He’s covered SEC Championships, Peach Bowls, Orange Bowls, Sugar Bowls, the Rose Bowl Game, College Football Playoff National Championship Games, the NCAA Tournament, the College World Series as well as a slew of college football, basketball and baseball games. Legge graduated from Coker College in 1999 with a degree in Political Science. He played both tennis and basketball for the Cobras. After graduating, Legge completed his academic career at the University of Georgia where he earned a Master of Public Administration from the School of Public and International Affairs in 2001. In 2008, Legge was elected President of the Coker College Alumni Association. He served on the Board of Trustees at Coker from 2009 to 2017 and was a member of the Executive Committee, Student Services and Enrollment Committee and Athletic Committee in that time. Legge is a native of Tucker, Georgia. It will feature ranked opponents for the first time since 2020. The No. 3 Bulldogs face a No. 20 Gators team at Mercedes-Benz Stadium Saturday in Atlanta. The game is being played outside of Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 due to stadium construction. First-year coach Jon Sumrall's Florida team smashed Ole Miss 52-28 to go to 4-0 before getting trounced by Missouri and South Carolina and then snagging another top 10 win at Texas. "Coach Sumrall's done a great job putting a lot of energy into the program, a lot of physicality in the program," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. "They play really hard. When you turn on the tape, you see the physicality they play with on both sides of the ball." Smart is 8-2 against Florida but 2-2 against ranked Florida teams, with the losses in 2016 and 2020. Georgia and Florida was a top 10 matchup for three straight years from 2018-2020 when Dan Mullen was Gators coach. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) is a half game behind first place Kentucky in the SEC standings and is coming off a 27-24 upset to unranked Auburn. "The message is just always never harp on one game or the past," Georgia linebacker Raylen Wilson said. "Just to learn from it and not to make the same mistakes." Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) is 2-1 on the road this season. Sumrall isn't viewing this game exactly as a neutral site. "We have to travel further so, yeah, it's more road-ish," he said. "It's in Atlanta. This is my first experience around this game. I know it's traditionally in Jacksonville. I think you have to know that Atlanta is not necessarily our backyard, right? But the 50-50 thing is a unique deal that I think is exciting for our guys because you're in kind of a different environment than a normal SEC game, which is fun." "How do we not turn the ball over? How do we stay away from dumb penalties? How do we tackle better?," Smart said. "How do we get more turnovers, so that our turnovers are less glaring? Georgia's offense and Gunner Stockton minimize turnovers and get the win. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. home.headline: Georgia’s new practice routine has made two Bulldogs’ injury status unknown
home.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
home.blurb: Kirby Smart detailed on Monday how Georgia handled their bye week differently this season. In the past they have continued to practice like normal with limited time off, but this year they only practiced on Tuesday and Thursday and had the rest of the week off. "Really don't know on either one of them because we haven't done anything since Thursday,” Kirby Smart said via 247Sports.com . “Those guys, we had good practices all week last week, and then leading into this week, we'll find out more about where they are today and through the injury report information we have.” Smart made it clear that he is willing to sacrifice some practice time to get his team healthy. In fact, this is something that Georgia has been doing all season because they have shortened each of their practices all season by 10 or 15 minutes. The goal in this is to help Georgia stay healthier without giving up too much preparation time, and so far it has worked out alright. The hope though is that guys like Isiah Canion and KJ Bolden could use this extra time off this week to get healthy so they can make their return against Florida this weekend, but Smart hasn't confirmed if they will be back yet or not. The hope is that this would help get Georgia as healthy as possible going into the rest of the season, but according to Smart on Monday it still isn't clear if wide receiver Isiah Canion or defensive back KJ Bolden will be healthy enough to play against Florida this weekend. Georgia’s new practice routine will hopefully pay off Georgia is 6-1 so they could be better off this season, but their record is still good enough to be the No. 3 team in the country. UGA has also had to deal with a handful of injuries throughout the season, but if you compare their injury report to other teams across the country they have had less injuries than others. Georgia desperately needs KJ Bolden back Georgia has only been without KJ Bolden for one game this season, and it just so happened to be their worst game of the year. UGA was without Bolden when they played Auburn two weeks ago and they were upset at home as the No. 1 team in the country. Who knows if Bolden could've changed that outcome if he was in the game, but it might not be a coincidence that Georgia's defense had their worst game of the season when he wasn't able to play. Georgia has been without Canion for longer, so they've already learned how to get by without him on offense. The same can't be said for Bolden though who is a projected first round pick at the upcoming NFL Draft this offseason. If Georgia wants their best shot at avoiding another upset they need Bolden back in the lineup to help slow down a Florida offense who is capable of scoring a lot of points. picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 28, 2026, 8:52 a.m. PT Oregon's national-title hopes have ended after a loss to Illinois dropped them to 4-3. Oregon will face a one-loss Northwestern team featuring former Ducks coach Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator. The Ducks' defense is expected to play well, but the offense faces a tough challenge against Northwestern. The Oregon football team's national title hopes are all but over, and it isn't even November. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview Chris Hansen Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 26, 2026, 5:14 a.m. PT The Oregon Ducks will host the No. 18 Northwestern Wildcats on Saturday, October 31. Northwestern's offense is led by former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly, who is now the offensive coordinator. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles is having a career-best season under Kelly's guidance. No time to wallow for Oregon's coaches and players. There's still lots of football left and against some pretty good teams. That includes this coming weekend. The Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten Conference) will host No. 18 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) and former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly at 12:30 p.m. Oct. 31. Kelly, who is in his first season as offensive coordinator on coach David Braun's staff, has the Wildcats humming. They are third in the Big Ten in total yards per game (435.6) and points (34.7) and are No. 2 in rushing yards per game (204.6). Northwestern is coming off a 42-14 win against Rutgers, the fourth straight win for the Wildcats since a 29-23 loss to Indiana on Sept. 25. The Ducks are coming off a 21-10 loss to Illinois that, barring a miracle, has ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff for a third straight season. On Sunday, Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . Here's an early look at Northwestern. Who is the Northwestern QB? The Wildcats have a familiar face at quarterback in Aidan Chiles, who previously played at Oregon State and Michigan State. The 6-foot-4, 225-pound dual-threat senior has been unlocked by Kelly and is having the best season of his career. Chiles has completed 117 of 164 passes for 1,617 yards and has 12 touchdowns to one interception. He's also rushed for a team-leading nine touchdowns. Last week against Rutgers he completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 83 yards and two touchdowns. He is the only player in the country to have multiple games of at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns this season. Other Northwestern offensive standouts Junior wide receiver Griffin Wilde has 39 catches for 615 yards and four touchdowns. In the game against Rutgers on Saturday, he had nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown. Running back Caleb Komolafe leads the Wildcats in rushing with 551 yards and five touchdowns on 88 carries. He also had a big game against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown on just 13 carries (11.5 yards per run). Joseph Himon II has been productive as well. He has 371 yards and three scores on 38 carries with an average of 9.8 yards per run. Defensive standouts for Northwestern Fifth-year Braydon Brus has been disruptive from his linebacker position, leading the team with 62 tackles, 11.0 tackles for loss and four sacks. He also has an interception and a fumble recovery. He is the conference co-leader in tackles and No. 2 in TFLs. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, a second-team all-conference player in 2025, is second on the team with 49 tackles and has a team-leading two interceptions, though he has missed the last two games with an injury. Fitzgerald’s 9.0 tackles per game leads the Big Ten. The last time the Ducks and Wildcats met Oregon and Northwestern have played each other just two times, and never before at Autzen Stadium. The Wildcats beat the Ducks in Evanston, Ill., in 1974, and last season Oregon came out on top 34-14. Dante Moore was 16-of-20 passing for 178 yards and a touchdown, and Dierre Hill Jr. had a 66-yard touchdown run in the third quarter as the Ducks built a 31-0 lead. All of Northwestern's points came in the fourth quarter after the Ducks pulled most of their starters. picks.headline: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma: Kickoff time, TV channel, injury report, odds
picks.blurb: Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here’s what you need to know about Saturday’s game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay’sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you’re making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren’t expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather’s 10-day forecast. There’s a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three’s a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven’t won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks’ SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven’t looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That’s certainly good, but USC’s running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn’t on Sellers’ legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina’s savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn’t necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC’s kicking competition this offseason. But he’s quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller’s absence because of injury. Hay’s Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer’s name this offseason, but he’s found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He’s got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer’s favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards. Email this person Michael Sauls is The State’s South Carolina women’s basketball reporter. away.blurb: On offense, key players like Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out for this week. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, that provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to their interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, but could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had some ups and downs for the Sooners over the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert product hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and saw fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotational linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. The other name to watch on the offensive line is center Jake Maikkula. Maikkula was injured in the win over Mississippi State and was replaced by Caleb Nitta. Nitta played well, and Oklahoma will need him again this week against the Gamecocks if Maikkula can't play. If Nitta gets the start, it would be the eighth straight game the Oklahoma Sooners have used a new starting offensive line combination. Also on offense, starting wide receiver Elijah Thomas won't be back this week after missing the Mississippi State game. That likely means another start for Manny Choice and perhaps Parker Livingstone when the Oklahoma Sooners are in three-wide receiver sets. home.headline: Oklahoma OT Michael Fasusi Expected to Return Against Mississippi State
home.blurb: Michael Fasusi was not listed on the final availability report ahead of OU's matchup against Mississippi State . He is projected to return to his starting spot at left tackle. The talented left tackle, who has missed every game since the Sooners' opener against UTEP, where he played only 17 snaps on offense per Pro Football Focus, was replaced by Ryan Fodje in OU's second game against Michigan. Fodje held the position over the next few weeks until his injury in last week's loss to Kentucky. Fodje is listed as out for today's game. Fasusi was initially listed as questionable on the SEC availability report on Wednesday. He was never upgraded on the Thursday and Friday reports. Eddy Pierre-Louis , a captain and starting left guard, has been out since appearing on the SEC availability report the week of the Texas game. He was in a cast on his right leg and used a single walking crutch. Pierre-Louis also missed last week's game against Kentucky and is out for today's game. Guard Heath Ozaeta was also not listed on the final availability report heading into the game with Mississippi State , meaning he will be available for the contest. Ozaeta appeared to injure his ankle during pregame warm-ups at the Cotton Bowl, but was able to play the entire game. Ozaeta missed last week and has been listed as questionable on this week's SEC availability reports. If he's available, he is projected to start at right guard. He has slowly ramped up his availability over the last few weeks as he deals with a right shoulder injury. In that game against UTEP, Fasusi was visibly dealing with the injury he sustained in Fall Camp. In his 17 offensive snaps, Fasusi was unable to lift or use his right arm in his final opportunities. Fasusi is a welcome addition to a depleted unit that has regressed both due to injuries and a lack of development. Fasusi could play alongside Noah Best , Jake Maikkula , and E'Marion Harris . If Ozaeta is unable to finish the game, he could be replaced by Peyton Joseph, who logged 69 offensive snaps in his first start of the season at right guard last week. home.headline: Oklahoma's Offense Turns in Best Game of the Season in Sooners' win at Mississippi State
home.blurb: It still wasn't perfect, and the Sooners still had to go down to the wire, but OU came out with a 23 -15 win over Mississippi State on Saturday in Stakrville, Miss. The left side of the offensive line was set with Michael Fasusi 's return. Unfortunately for the Sooners, Bowen took a big hit on his interception return and was banged up. His status moving forward is unknown. But Oklahoma held the Bulldogs with just nine return yards and no field-goal tries. Oklahoma's offense took a significant step forward Saturday. John Mateer protected the ball, the Sooners had a strong rushing attack, and the defense did what it needed to do against former Oklahoma offensive coordinator Jeff Lebby 's Bulldogs. Here's a look at a much more balanced edition of the positional report card: John Mateer had by far his best game of the season, Mateer's day was punctuated by his dive on third-and-5 after he couldn't find an open receiver and instead scrambled for the first down, diving for the line-to-gain and holding onto the football. Then he hit tight end Rocky Beers for a 13-yard completion on third down to put the game away. Mateer finished 22 of 29 for a season-high 283 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions and had nine carries for 37 yards. If Mateer can play like this the rest of the season, the Sooners season figures to look much, much better. On the touchdown drive late in the second quarter that sent Oklahoma into the locker room up 10-0, Mateer was 6 for 7 and had three critical runs to keep the drive alive. Offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said earlier this week that Tory Blaylock was rounding into the form which made him the Sooners' leading rushter last season as a freshman. Arbuckle's observation looked spot on as Blaylock broke off a 47-yard run on the first play of the second half. Blaylock finished with 71 yards on 12 carries, more than doubling his production from the first six games. It wasn't just Blaylock, though. Lloyd Avant ran for 55 yards on 13 carries, including a 19-yard carry. The Sooners finished with a season-high 184 yards on the ground. Isaiah Sategna continues to prove himself as a top-flight receiver. He had none only eight catches for 164 yards and a touchdown — a 36-yarder in the second quarter — but also had three carries for 24 yards as Arbuckle used the star receiver in the running game as well with some motions and other wrinkles to spread the field horizontally. But the rest of the wide receivers had just three catches for 14 yards as the tight ends and running backs made up the bulk of the production in the passing game outside of Sategna. Jer'Michael Carter had a 6-yard catch, Manny Choice and Jacob Jordan had catches of three yards. But at least Mateer spread the ball around, and the Sooners would take this type of performance all day long. About the only things that keep this from being an A is Rocky Beers ' fumble that gave the Bulldogs the ball early in the third quarter and Beers' drop of a potential touchdow

home.headline: Rapid Reaction: Oklahoma Sooners beat Mississippi State 23-15
home.blurb: Isaiah Sategna led the receiving corps with eight receptions for 164 yards and a touchdown. His second-half touchdown seemed to spark the Sooners' offense coming out of halftime. FINAL: Oklahoma Sooners close out win, 23-15 The Oklahoma Sooners got the ball back with just over two minutes to play and John Mateer came through on a pair of critical third downs. First, running and diving for the first down to open the drive. Then, on third-and-11, Mateer rolled out and hit Beers for a 13-yard completion to get the final first down, allowing the Sooners to kneel the ball and close out the win. The Sooners defense has played great for most of the game but it's going to be on the offense to go close it out under two minutes. John Mateer hit Isaiah Sategna for a big play and the Oklahoma Sooners looked like they had a touchdown when Mateer hit Beers in the end zone, but the ball was knocked out of his hands late, after the play seemed dead, and the referees deemed it incomplete. Tate Sandell kicked his second field goal of the game to make it 20-7. The Oklahoma Sooners got the ball back after a punt and were moving out of their own end of the field after a couple of first downs. Mateer hit Rocky Beers for a big gain, but when Beers tried to hurdle the defender, the ball came out and was recovered by Mississippi State. Explosive out of the half: Sooners lead 17-0 - 13:44, third quarter The Oklahoma Sooners went three-and-out for the first time today. Mateer hit Hayden Hansen on second down and hit Jonathan Hatton on the dump-off on third down but was tackled short of the first-down marker. Mississippi State broke into Sooners' territory on a big run from Fluff Bothwell. But that's all they could muster on the drive. A deep ball to Anthony Evans was just out of his reach and Reggie Powers III stopped Evans for a loss on a wide receiver screen. On fourth-and-6, Kamario Taylor attempted to break out of the pocket and pick up the yardage with his legs, but came up hobbling due to the turf toe injury on his right foot. Owen Heinecke was able to run him to the sideline for the sack and turnover on downs. For the first time since Week 1, projected starting left tackle Michael Fasusi will be available for the Oklahoma Sooners. With Ryan Fodje, who started the last five games at left tackle ruled out earlier in the week, expect Fasusi to return to his spot on John Mateer's blindside. Guard Heath Ozaeta is also available to play this week. He could take back his spot at right guard, where he started in the Sooners' win over Texas. Peyton Joseph could also start at guard again. Starting corner Eli Bowen and starting wide receiver Elijah Thomas will be out for this week as well, meaning Trystan Haynes will make his third consecutive start since taking over before the Texas game. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). Clemson football odds of reaching bowl game after brutal Week 7 loss to Virginia Tech In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 78.1%, down from 88.4% prior to its loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson's chances of winning its final five games are just 2.1%, according to ESPN's FPI. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. away.headline: Two FSU freshmen trending toward returning vs. Clemson
away.blurb: Crutchfield has been in and out of FSU's lineup this season as he battles injuries, but the coaching staff has been extremely pleased with what he can do, and Norvell is "hopeful" he will be available this week. "I think Jordan Crutchfield is trending well to be able to get back in the secondary," Norvell said. "We've had some guys that have been banged up there as well. Jordan's a guy that has shown some flashes here, just dealt with some minor injuries that have kind of set him back just from the consistency of his opportunities, but expecting him to get some good work here this week and hopefully be available." The update was less positive about Nichelson, who hasn't played since the game against the New Mexico State Aggies, and Norvell doesn't expect that to change this week. He is "hopeful" that the rest of the linebackers will be able to play after several were in and out of the Miami game with injuries. Head coach Mike Norvell spoke with the media on Monday and provided an injury update ahead of Saturday's game against the Clemson Tigers , specifically mentioning freshman wide receiver Devin Carter, linebacker Blake Nichelson, and freshman defensive back Jordan Crutchfield. Carter, who the coaching staff praised all offseason, has not played this season after hurting his back and ribs during the preseason. That could be changing soon, per Norvell. "Devin Carter is coming into having an opportunity this week, barring any setbacks, we'll see where that goes," Norvell said. "You'll see what that looks like, another explosive player that brings opportunity." home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players.
