You don't start 7-0, score nearly 50 points a game and climb to No. 1 by accident. But there's something about laying more than two touchdowns on the road that makes me uncomfortable, especially against a North Carolina team that's been hanging around with some decent opponents. Miami probably wins this game. I'd be surprised if it didn't. But asking the Hurricanes to go into Chapel Hill and win by 17? That's a different bet altogether. Be ready for all the college football action with our free college football picks . Miami heads to Kenan Memorial Stadium in Chapel Hill on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM ET on ABC. The Hurricanes opened as 14.5-point favorites, with some books now showing 15.5. Our original betting numbers were North Carolina +16.5 and Under 51.5. That extra point on the spread matters, and I wouldn't pretend every sportsbook is still offering it. This is an outdoor game, so I'll want another look at the Chapel Hill weather forecast before kickoff, particularly the wind and any chance of rain. Miami Hurricanes Have the Offense to Put This Away Early Miami is 7-0, including 3-0 away from home, and just beat Pittsburgh 52-23. The Hurricanes have scored 43 or more in three of their last four games, and they've already beaten Clemson 41-13 on the road. That's a pretty good argument for laying the points, I'll give you that. Pittsburgh couldn't do much with Miami's passing game Saturday. The Hurricanes scored 52, and the scary part is that they still left some plays out there. North Carolina isn't going to survive if it spends the first half giving Miami short fields and easy touchdowns. The numbers explain why the Hurricanes are such a big favorite. They're averaging 49 points and 552 yards per game. Nobody in the country is producing more total offense. Miami throws for about 341 yards a game and runs for another 211, so taking away one part of the offense doesn't necessarily solve anything. Defensively, the Hurricanes allow just 15.3 points and 60 rushing yards per game. Sixty. That's going to make life difficult for a North Carolina offense that hasn't run the ball particularly well. Miami also converts 54.5% of its third downs. If the Tar Heels can't get the Hurricanes off the field, that home crowd won't have much to cheer about. Sign Up Get $30 Premium Picks Credit + Exclusive Offers Darian Mensah is having one heck of a season. He's thrown for 2,151 yards with 22 touchdowns and just one interception, completing better than 81% of his passes. Against Pittsburgh, he went 31-for-37 for 387 yards and four scores. Malachi Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns in that game, giving him 952 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Javian Mallory has added 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. That's plenty of offense for North Carolina to worry about. Miami does have some injuries, with receiver Jalen Moore and running back Chris Brown out for the season. Tight end Logan Gilbert is also sidelined, while Owen Ruskavich's status needs checking. But the Hurricanes haven't had much trouble scoring without them. North Carolina Tar Heels Need to Make Miami Earn Everything North Carolina is 4-3 overall and 1-2 at home. The Tar Heels had won two straight before losing 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime Saturday. That one had to sting. They had a chance to get their fifth win and instead let Syracuse walk out of Chapel Hill with it. Still, I wouldn't throw out everything North Carolina has done because of one ugly finish. The Tar Heels beat Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and followed it with a 24-20 win at Duke. They also played Clemson to an eight-point game. Those aren't the results of a team that rolls over every time it sees a better opponent. The offense is the problem. North Carolina averages 24.4 points and 336 yards per game, and the running game produces only 114 yards a night. That's not much help against Miami's defensive front. The Tar Heels are probably going to have to throw more than they'd like. Defensively, though, they've allowed 20.9 points per game. That's respectable, even if the 373 yards they're giving up tells you opponents are moving the ball. What worries me most is third down. North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.1% of the time. Miami is one of the best third-down teams in the country. That's a bad matchup, and Bill Belichick has to find a way to get his defense off the field before the Hurricanes start piling up possessions. Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,530 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He passed for 271 yards and two scores against Syracuse, so he can move the ball when he gets protection. Jordan Shipp has 543 receiving yards, including eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown Saturday. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards, while Demon June has seven rushing touchdowns. The Tar Heels are dealing with some injuries at receiver, including Carnell Warren and Kaden Chapman, and they're missing tight ends Jordan Washington and Jake Warren. That's not ideal when you're facing a defense as good as Miami's. But Edwards has enough experience to keep North Carolina from becoming completely one-dimensional. Miami vs North Carolina Picks and Predictions North Carolina Tar Heels +16.5 I'm taking North Carolina +16.5, assuming that number is still available. I know Miami could make this look foolish in a hurry. The Hurricanes have the better quarterback, the better offense and a defense that barely lets anybody run the ball. But sixteen and a half points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that's been competitive with Clemson, Pittsburgh and Duke. North Carolina has lost three games, and two of those defeats came by eight points or fewer. The Tar Heels also have a quarterback who can throw well enough to put together a late scoring drive if they're down a couple of touchdowns. That's what I'm looking for here. Miami can control most of the game and still fail to cover a number this big. I wouldn't be surprised by a 30-17 or 34-20 Miami win. Either one gets the job done for North Carolina backers at +16.5. At +14.5, though, I like it considerably less. I'll take Under 51.5, although this is the pick that makes me a little nervous. Miami is averaging 49 points a game by itself, and that's not something you can just ignore. But North Carolina isn't built to get into a scoring contest with the Hurricanes. The Tar Heels need to run some clock, avoid turnovers and make Miami work for its points. They can't afford to turn this into a game where both teams are snapping the ball every twenty seconds. Miami's defense should help us here because the Hurricanes allow only 15.3 points per game and have been excellent against the run. If North Carolina finishes somewhere around 14 or 17 points, Miami can score into the low 30s without pushing this over. The danger is an early Miami explosion or a couple of defensive touchdowns. That's real. But I think the Tar Heels will try to slow the game down, and Miami's defense should keep North Carolina from doing too much scoring. Give me Miami 31-17. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him. Freshman wide receiver Milan Parris was ruled out of last Saturday's 52-23 win over Pitt with an undisclosed injury. He was not listed on the initial injury report. Parris hasn't carved out a consistent role, playing just 54 offensive snaps through five games played out of seven. The Tar Heels are without starting cornerback Tre Miller (undisclosed). The redshirt junior will be sidelined for a third consecutive game. Starting safety Peyton Waters (undisclosed), who hasn't played since facing Duke on Oct. 17, is listed as questionable. It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. After a bye week, the Buckeyes will now be facing off against the USC Trojans, giving this team another test to overcome. Ohio State remains one of the better teams in the country, but the Trojans will be a challenge. This will be the first game between the two historic programs in Big Ten play, giving each another reason to want to win. The two programs have met multiple times over the years, and it's always been a fun matchup. The Buckeyes did lose starting quarterback Julian Sayin, likely for the season, but this team still has a lot of talent on the roster. Ohio State believes that it can still win a title this season, and the Trojans are just the next team in its way. As the team gets ready for the Trojans, they will be entering the game with a record of 6-1, going 4-0 in Big Ten play. USC comes in with a record of 6-2, going 3-2 in their conference games so far. The Trojans are coming off a bad loss to the Wisconsin Badgers last weekend, giving this team all the desperation they need. The Buckeyes will need to stay focused in this game, looking at this trip as purely business. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are still favored to take down the Trojans, even with the injury to Sayin. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has an 82.8 percent chance of defeating USC on the road this week. For the Buckeyes, making sure to keep the basics the same in this game will be a key. Even without Sayin, the offense should still run through star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, giving the team a boost. Ohio State may rely even more heavily on Smith to help whoever is under center for this Buckeyes team, giving them a reliable target. Smith is on pace for a truly special season, and the loss of Sayin shouldn't change that fact. The Buckeyes defense will also be tasked with slowing down USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, who has thrown for 2,302 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Trojans rely on their offense to set the tone for the team, and the defense has been a little shaky this season. Kickoff between the two sides is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

Finally, to close it all out, we'll take a look at a Big Ten tilt between the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes and USC Trojans. Baylor has fired head coach Dave Aranda, a move made after a critical loss to Kansas in Week 8. The former LSU defensive coordinator leaves Waco with a 40-40 overall mark, not good enough for the current administration. Former athletic director Mack Rhoades took a separation agreement in November 2025, leaving Aranda's future in doubt under new athletic director Doug McNamee. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman, recently brought in from Kansas State , will serve as the interim coach as Baylor looks to reach bowl season. The Baylor defense was never the issue this season, allowing an average of 16.1 points per game. The offense, under transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, has severely struggled with coordinator Jake Spavital. The Bears sit outside the top 110 in Success Rate on offense, relying on pass explosives as the only means of creating scoring opportunities. Despite the struggles as a whole, Lagway has seen improvement from his days at Florida with an increase in big-time throws and a lower turnover-worthy play rate. The Bears struggle in scoring position, averaging just 3.3 points on 50 offensive possessions inside the opponent's 40-yard line. Red-zone efficiency has been a constant failure all season, ranking 121st in touchdown percentage. Only half of the 30 possessions that made it into the red zone have resulted in a Baylor touchdown. UCF had one of the more advantageous spots of the entire college football calendar when hosting BYU , as the Cougars were coming off a program-defining win over Notre Dame . The overtime game provided all the thrills for a college football masterpiece, as the Knights took a field-storming victory with an 89% post-game win expectancy. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins led UCF to four methodical drives and an explosive passing attack, tossing six explosives through the air. The defense had the assignment of slowing down Heisman hopeful Bear Bachmeier , and it limited the BYU quarterback to just 37 rushing yards on 15 carries. The biggest factor was basic fundamentals, as the Knights missed just nine tackles in the game to add on a PFF tackling grade that ranks in the top 25. The Cougars' high-octane offense was limited to just a single rush explosive. It makes sense considering UCF's defense ranks 15th in Line Yards and top-40 in Rush EPA allowed. The handicap on this game forces handicappers to look beyond the advanced statistics, as the Baylor program is in flux. Klanderman isn't expected to win the job as Baylor's head coach, as McNamee has made it clear a coach with Texas roots and an offensive mindset will be the next hire. The downstream effect of the coaching search could create outside noise for coordinators and players looking for their next stop if they don't make a bowl game. Statistically, Baylor could have a hard time generating points against the UCF defense. The Bears have generated plenty of available yards to create scoring opportunities, but a rank outside the top 100 in Finishing Drives will go against a Knights defense that's 32nd in limiting opponents in scoring position. With the expectation that UCF will have a hangover from one of the most electric college football games of the season, a first-half under is the look from a statistical and spot perspective. There are also advantages for UCF in the run game against the Baylor defense. The Bears have a top-10 unit in terms of Rushing Success Rate allowed but have a mid-FBS average of 50% against teams that use inside zone. The Knights run a heavy amount of inside zone through Jenkins and running back Duke Watson . A boost could be in store if quarterback Alonza Barnett III returns from a hamstring injury. The James Madison transfer suited up for the BYU game but did not play for the fifth straight game. Any contribution from Barnett would further solidify UCF's position. Pick: 1H Under 24.5 · UCF ML (-110 or Better) Florida entered the bye week on a high note, beating a top-10 team on the road for the first time since 2012. The Gators remain at two losses on the season in the thick of the SEC race and a potential spot in the College Football Playoff, but a date with Georgia in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party comes first. The biggest takeaway from the victory over Texas came from backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. tossing a couple of touchdowns in a mistake-free game. The sophomore completed 22-of-35 passes while chipping in 50 rushing yards with an even split of scrambles and designed run calls. On the other side, the defense continues to rank as one of the best in the nation when creating chaos. The top-10 Havoc numbers are led by 53 tackles for loss , nine forced fumbles and 34 passes defensed. Five players on the defensive line have generated double-digit pressures, while seven different defenders have multiple pass breakups. The issue with Florida's defense is its performance close to the goal line, ranking 95th in red-zone defense. The Gators have allowed 40 opponent possessions to cross the 40-yard line and are giving up an average of 4.4 points per trip . Georgia's first loss to Auburn in nine years comes as a result of ball protection. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was responsible for two interceptions and a fumble, an uncharacteristic set of events for the senior. Up until the Alabama game in Week 6, Stockton managed to throw just six interceptions and lose three fumbles since the beginning of the 2025 season. In the past two games, the Georgia quarterback has committed two fumbles and three interceptions . There's the case that Stockton had too much of the load against Auburn, taking a critical hit in the first series of the game. Running back Chauncey Bowens has missed multiple games with injury, while Nate Frazier was ineffective coming off a rib injury, finishing with less than 20 rushing yards. The bye week should provide the best health for the offense in weeks, as head coach Kirby Smart described Bowens as day-to-day . Stockton should also be fully recovered from any shoulder or concussion symptoms. The Bulldogs defense continues to be one of the best nationally in defending the run, ranking top-25 in Rushing Success Rate allowed and Defensive Line Yards. Georgia grades out as one of the best tackling teams nationally, as no individual player has missed more than five tackles this season . Cornerback Ellis Robinson IV has been one of the best at shutting down wideouts all season with five pass breakups and an interception. Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has been excellent in disguising blitzes this season, as the highest tally of pressures this season comes from linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson. The Gators have struggled to run the ball of late, posting a Stuff Rate above the national average in the last three SEC contests against Texas, South Carolina and Missouri . Florida has three primary run concepts in the arsenal: outside zone, counter and power. The most successful and explosive of the group comes from power attempts with a heavy box, led by running back Jadan Baugh. The junior has 100 more rushing attempts than any other player on the team, running an even split of zone read and non-zone read concepts. Despite the highly successful numbers against zone read and counter, Georgia has been horrific against power concepts this season . The Bulldogs have elite numbers in Defensive Finishing Drives and red-zone prevention, ranking fifth in red-zone drives allowed. Although only 15 drives have passed the Georgia 20, the Bulldogs have allowed 14 scores, with 11 of the 15 drives resulting in a touchdown . On the other side of the ball, Georgia has been a pure zone-read team with a heavy batch of inside zone with 11 and 12 personnel. Nearly every run concept from the Bulldogs comes in well above the national average in Success Rate and EPA, but inside and outside zone read produce an explosive on one of every five attempts. Florida has been successful against outside zone but has yet to see an offense execute with two-tight end sets. Georgia should thrive in passing downs, as the Gators sit outside the top 90 in Success Rate and EPA allowed when opponents are off schedule . Florida has been putrid at keeping opponents out of scoring position and the end zone this season. On the other side, Georgia defense has been dominated by power run concepts, so Baugh should find a way to put Florida on the board. away.headline: What is the status of Ohio State's Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Jay Timmons?
away.blurb: "Last week was a great opportunity to get a bunch of guys some rest," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "We'll see how this week goes. ... [Most] will probably go through the rest of the week, and as we get closer to the game, we'll get an idea." Jackson was helped to the medical tent by two Ohio State athletic trainers with 11:55 remaining in the Buckeyes ' 19-15 road win on Oct. 17. He returned for the Hoosiers' final drive but then had to be helped by defensive tackle Eddrick Houston and a trainer going back to the locker room. The fifth-year defender provides crucial experience, as he's the only remaining Ohio State defensive lineman who appeared in all 16 games during the 2024 national championship run. Along with leading the Buckeyes in sacks this season (3), Jackson has played 320 snaps, according to PFF – 63 more than any other Ohio State defensive lineman. Of Jackson's 22 tackles, seven came against the Hoosiers, marking his career high. Timmons also had a career game in Bloomington, recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble, before being sidelined for Ohio State's final defensive drives. The freshman was dealing with an unspecified injury leading up to the Indiana game, missing the previous two matchups. In his first four Ohio State games, Timmons logged nine tackles, four pass breakups and a forced fumble in the opening drive against Texas. He was initially hurt in the third quarter against Illinois on Sept. 26. No. 2 Ohio State will travel to face No. 15 Southern California on Oct. 31.

The matchup between the Gophers and the Hoosiers is a rather interesting choice, given that Minnesota is unranked, Indiana is favored by nearly three touchdowns, and ESPN is not even televising the game. Kenyatta Jackson, defensive end Jackson was hurt late in Ohio State’s win at Indiana on Oct. 17. home.headline: “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss
home.blurb: In recent weeks, there had been speculation that ESPN's "College GameDay" could finally return to Los Angeles for the matchup of college football blue bloods. After USC's performance in Madison, however, that possibility went out the window, and "GameDay" will instead head to Minnesota- Indiana . Someday, "College GameDay" will finally return to USC. Right now, however, it appears as though that return will be under a different head coach. “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Milwaukee can finally celebrate Jokić's 200th triple-double “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads On Saturday evening, the USC football team suffered an embarrassing 24-7 road loss to Wisconsin . This week, however, the Trojans will be back home at the Coliseum to take on Ohio State. The matchup between the Gophers and the Hoosiers is a rather interesting choice, given that Minnesota is unranked, Indiana is favored by nearly three touchdowns, and ESPN is not even televising the game. This strongly suggests that the show had another game in mind, but had to pivot at the last minute due to an upset. In other words, USC had an absolutely golden opportunity to finally bring "GameDay" back to the Coliseum for the first time in 13 years—an astonishing streak for one of the premier programs in the sport. However, Lincoln Riley blew it, and instead, the drought will continue. From 2004 through 2013, the Trojans hosted "GameDay" at least once in all but two years—including twice in 2006. However, due to a combination of down years for the program and ESPN placing an increased emphasis on the SEC, "GameDay" has not returned to the Coliseum since USC upset Stanford in 2013. UCF enters Week 9 fresh off the biggest win in program history, while Baylor navigates the fallout from firing its head coach. Now, the Knights have a massive target on their backs as they draw a Baylor team that just fired head coach Dave Aranda after nearly seven seasons. There's nothing more glorious than the coach-firing bump . This Knights team isn't all that impressive, either. Outside of Week 8, UCF hasn't been competitive against quality competition, with losses to Pitt, Houston, and Oklahoma State. Its other three wins came against TCU, Georgia State, and Bethune-Cookman. With that win over BYU clearly serving as its Super Bowl, the Knights should regress this week against the Bears. Baylor or nothing. Take the Bears on the moneyline if you don't want to lay any juice. UCF ranks 118th nationally in passing yards allowed per game , giving Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway a chance to carve up this mediocre pass defense. Even with the Bears' stout defense, the Knights should still find a way to get on the board. In the end, though, Baylor should do most of the heavy lifting to push this total over the finish line. picks.blurb: Baylor vs UCF Prediction: Who Can Build Off the Moment? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers win World Series Milwaukee can finally celebrate Dybantsa delivers in NBA debut WNBA Finals fatigue Jokić's 200th triple-double Baylor vs UCF Prediction: Who Can Build Off the Moment? Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective. Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12); UCF (4-3, 2-2). Last meeting: Baylor beat UCF 30-3 on Nov. 1, 2025, in Waco What's at stake? This is an important opportunity for Baylor to get its season back on track. The Bears have dropped consecutive games against TCU and Kansas and now enter a new chapter under interim head coach Joe Klanderman following Dave Aranda's dismissal . At 4-3, Baylor cannot afford to let another conference game slip away if it hopes to remain competitive in the Big 12 standings. A road win would also give Klanderman a strong start to his tenure. UCF enters the matchup with momentum after defeating No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime. The Knights have shown they can compete with the conference's top teams, making Friday's matchup an important test for Baylor's defense. When Baylor has the ball Baylor's passing attack will be one of its biggest advantages in this matchup. The Bears average 278.9 passing yards per game, and UCF surrenders 239.7 passing yards per game. Quarterback DJ Lagway will need to take advantage of that matchup and find opportunities downfield. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has been one of Baylor's most consistent weapons, recording 58 receptions for 678 yards through seven games. His ability to create plays and stretch the field could be important against a UCF defense that has struggled more against the pass than the run. However, Baylor will need to establish a more consistent rushing attack. Dawson Pendergrass leads the Bears with 331 rushing yards, but the offense has averaged just 146.1 rushing yards per game. Finding balance between the run and pass will be important in keeping UCF's defense from focusing entirely on Lagway. When UCF has the ball The Knights rely on a balanced offensive attack led by quarterback Keyone Jenkins and running back Duke Watson. Jenkins has thrown for 1,099 yards and 11 touchdowns while Watson leads the team with 577 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Baylor's defensive front will need to pressure Jenkins and limit Watson's ability to establish the run. The Bears rank third nationally in sacks, giving them an opportunity to disrupt UCF's offensive rhythm. If Baylor can force third-and-long situations and create turnovers, it could make things difficult for a UCF offense that is coming off an emotional double-overtime victory. Baylor enters this matchup with plenty to prove after consecutive losses and a coaching change. While UCF has momentum following its win over BYU, the Bears have the defensive talent to make this a difficult matchup for the Knights. I expect Baylor to lean on its defense and take advantage of its passing game, with Freeman playing an important role. The Bears will need to clean up their mistakes and avoid giving UCF extra opportunities, but the Bears will find a way to get their first win under Klanderman. Score: Baylor 27, UCF 24. UCF enters the game riding high after stunning No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime for the Knights' biggest win since joining the Big 12. Meanwhile, Baylor is beginning a new era after firing head coach Dave Aranda following Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim head coach. Despite taking very different paths to get here, Baylor and UCF enter Friday night's game with identical 4-3 overall records and 2-2 marks in Big 12 play. For UCF, the question is whether Scott Frost's team can build off its breakthrough win or suffer a letdown. For Baylor, it's about what kind of response the Bears will have in their first game without Aranda. Here is everything you need to know about Baylor vs. UCF in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Friday night's Big 12 matchup. Baylor vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 48.5 Moneyline: UCF -120/Baylor +100 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: How do the emotions play a factor? The emotions on both sides of this game are tremendous. UCF is coming off of one of the biggest wins in program history over No. 2 BYU in double overtime at home. Now, they have to put that in the rearview mirror and take on Baylor. What' done is done. Have the Knights spent the last week in celebration mode? And then, on the other side, head coach Dave Aranda was fired on Sunday by Baylor. How does the team respond? How does defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman do in the interim role? There are so many unknowns going into this game, beyond the X's and O's, that ultimately will determine the outcome. Baylor vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: UCF 23, Baylor 20 It's a short week for both teams, but the good news for UCF is that they're playing their second-straight home game after a bye week. They haven't had to leave the friendly confines of Central Florida in nearly a month. Meantime, Baylor is getting set for its 3rd road game in its last four match ups, and their first without Aranda. In games like this, I try to find a nugget to sway me one way or the other, and here's what I've found: Baylor leads the Big 12 with 27 sacks in seven games. But one of the many things that UCF has done well with Keyone Jenkins is move the pocket, get rid of the ball quickly and avoid pressure in the backfield. BYU only had one sack last week against UCF, and the Knights have only allowed 10 in seven games, good for fourth fewest in the Big 12 Conference. Negating the pass rush by Baylor opens up a lot of opportunities for the UCF offense, and I believe that will be a game-changer on Friday night. Baylor has proven it can play with, and beat, some of the lesser Big 12 teams like Colorado and Arizona State. But even against just slightly better competition, TCU and Kansas, they came up short. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images College Football Week 9 Friday night college football previews. Baylor vs. UCF Three games are on the college football card for Friday night, headlined by Baylor vs. UCF. Both teams are in very difficult spots here, as the Knights just upset BYU at home in overtime last week and the Bears fired head coach Dave Aranda after losing at home to Kansas. On a night with the MAC, American, and Big 12, we have Kent State as a rare home favorite, a mediocre Tulane team laying double digits, and then the coin flip in Orlando. Despite the tricky circumstances with Baylor and UCF, that’s the game of the night and the game that deserves the most attention. Odds from Circa Sports as of October 28, 1:20 p.m. PT ; check out our Circa Betting Splits and DraftKings Betting Splits . See all of our Week 9 College Football Picks and Predictions . Baylor at UCF (-1, 48) Prediction Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Baylor invades the Bounce House this week and we’ll see if interim head coach Joe Klanderman can put some more pep in the steps of the Bears. It felt like Aranda was simply holding on for dear life with this gig for a while and it finally came to a head this past week with a blocked field goal that led to a loss against the Jayhawks. I watched Klanderman’s media availability this week and he comes across as a very honest, very poignant guy who isn’t going to BS this team about what’s going on. I appreciate that. In this day and age, I think the players do as well. Klanderman will continue to call the defense, while longtime up-and-comer Jake Spavital has creative freedom on offense. The 41-year-old Spavital was Texas A&M’s OC by the age of 30 and even was Texas State’s head coach for four rough seasons. But he’s always been pretty highly-regarded in the coaching world and now he has free reign of the offense. By no means has the offense been good, but Aranda was kind of a passive guy and there wasn’t a lot of explosiveness or aggressiveness to Baylor’s offensive profile. With a lot of money invested in DJ Lagway, let’s see if Spavital can unlock something. Lagway has only completed 52.1% of his passes and only has 26 carries for 19 yards, so it’s been a struggle to get him free. Leading rusher Dawson Pendergrass only has 3.5 yards per carry. The Baylor offensive line needs to be better, but we should see an improvement in effort and focus for this week. UCF head coach Scott Frost brought in Keyone Jenkins as an insurance policy behind expected starter Alonza Barrett III from James Madison. Instead, it has been Jenkins, the FIU transfer, who has carried this team in Barrett’s absence. He sports an 11/3 TD/INT ratio and a completion rate butting up against 70%, while transfer RB Duke Watson has rushed for 6.8 yards per carry. While Baylor’s defensive numbers stand up a lot better, as the Bears are 17th in the nation in yards per play allowed, it should be noted that Jeff Sagarin has a strength of schedule gap of 30 spots between the two teams, as UCF has already played three top-30 teams per Sagarin and Baylor has not played any. The Knights rank 27th in SOS and the Bears are 57th, with a big difference in Big 12 opponents. UCF has played TCU, Houston, Oklahoma State, and BYU. Baylor has played Colorado, Arizona State, TCU, and Kansas. Of that group, Arizona State is the only one with a winning record and the only one without a losing conference record. It’s a tough spot for UCF coming off of the BYU win, but they aren’t traveling, they don’t have the internal tumult, and Jenkins has definitively outplayed Lagway this season and even done so against better competition. Other Friday Games Tulane (-10, 47) at Charlotte: This is a hefty number for Tulane, a team that ranks 99th with -.51 net points per drive per Brian Fremeau of BCFToys. Of course, Charlotte is 134th out of 138 teams, so we’re talking about one of the worst programs in the nation. The Green Wave have not gotten good QB play out of either Kadin Semonza or Trace Johnson, with 18 total sacks and a 5/5 TD/INT ratio. Even though the Green Wave have a great running game and maybe that will be enough, winning by margin requires taking care of the football and avoiding negative plays. Charlotte has poor run defense numbers, but it should be noted that they’ve allowed 4.55 YPC to FBS opponents and allowed 5.36 YPC in the loss to The Citadel. Kent State (-10, 46.5) at Sacramento State: Historical outliers are scary and Kent State being favored like this on the road hasn’t happened since 2022. That could be part of the reason why we’ve seen money come in on the Hornets and against the Golden Flashes. It’s also just ludicrous to think about Kent State facing these kinds of expectations, but Sac State might be the worst FBS team we’ve ever seen. If Kent wins and covers, that might solidify it, but that’s an enormous ask and the market seems to think it’s too big of one. So, whether Spell suits up on Friday against Baylor will be telling on his availability going forward. However, there was one offensive lineman ruled out for Friday: Tyler Gibson . It is set to be his third consecutive missed game. After making his 2026 debut on Saturday against BYU, Duane Thomas Jr. is now designated as probable for Friday's matchup against Baylor. Plus, the Knights do not necessarily have to rush him back to a central role, given the target shares Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes and Waden Charles have accumulated. Meanwhile, after missing two games, sophomore Caleb Rollerson now has an opening to return to the field on Friday after being ruled questionable on Tuesday. Despite optimism from Frost on Monday about him being "really close," Lewis Carter has been ruled out for a fifth consecutive game. Jennings was also listed in Tuesday's report, designated as probable . However, it is still going to keep Swint out for at least one more week, which provides another opportunity for Landen Chambers to earn more carries out of the backfield, which he took advantage of against BYU. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. Following a BYU three-and-out, the Knights went 62 yards in eight plays, highlighted by Duke Watson's 30-yard rush. UCF, meanwhile, went three-and-out to start the game. Duke Watson gained 5 yards on his first carry, followed by a pair of incomplete passes from Keyone Jenkins. Barnett has not played since Sept. 12. He went through warmups in uniform today, though, after being listed as a game-time decision. Barnett is listed as a game-time decision. He has not played since Sept. 12 against Pitt. Alonza Barnett III listed as game-time decision UCF quarterback Alonza Barnett III (hamstring) is officially listed as a game-time decision for Saturday's showdown with BYU on the Big 12 Conference's final availability report. He is joined by redshirt freshman center Jacob Maiava (groin), who missed the road game against Oklahoma State. Slot receiver Duane Thomas Jr. was removed from the report, meaning he will make his 2026 debut after sitting out the first six games with a nagging hamstring problem. James Madison transfer Alonza Barnett III has been out since he injured his hamstring Sept. 12 at Pittsburgh, but he was listed as questionable on the injury report leading up to today's game. However, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported earlier in the week that he would remain out. If Barnett can't go, FIU transfer Keyone Jenkins would be in line for his fifth straight start. AccuWeather predicts 79 degrees with partly cloudy skies at kickoff in Orlando, Florida. Winds are expected to blow out of the north-northeast at 15 mph. There is about a 50% chance of rain. But boy, they did more than that on homecoming in the Acrisure Bounce House. UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) upset the previously undefeated BYU Cougars (6-1, 3-1) in a weird, wild and wacky contest that ended 39-31 in double overtime. It was the Knights ' first-ever home victory over a top-10 opponent. It included a topsy-turvy final minute of regulation in which everyone in the building experienced the full range of emotions. Once overtime arrived, the teams traded touchdowns. Keyone Jenkins put UCF ahead in double OT with a 4-yard touchdown toss to Grayson Brousseau and then found Tyren Hornes for a two-point conversion. home.headline: UCF Defensive Back Ruled Out vs. Baylor: Injury Report Breakdown
home.blurb: UCF Defensive Back Ruled Out vs. Baylor: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM However, Alonza Barnett III 's name is back in the report, designated as questionable . Frost said he thought Barnett "probably could play," but he did not know if he was 100%. Should he be able to play, he could serve as an emergency backup to Jenkins should he get injured during the game. The Knights' secondary took another hit this week as starting safety Demari Henderson has been ruled out for Friday's Space Game. It will be the first time Henderson has missed a game since he missed a majority of the 2024 season. He joins cornerback DJ Bell , who was ruled out for a second straight week. Maiava was designated as probable and was a game-time decision against BYU, so he is trending towards returning on Friday. Fellow offensive lineman Preston Cushman was also designated probable. Meanwhile, Spell's name is nowhere to be found in Tuesday's report, which could mean one of two things: he is available to play on Friday, or he has been designated out for the season. Frost said back on Sep. 19 that Spell had "a bit of plantar fasciitis," a condition that has different recovery times depending on the severity. So, whether Spell suits up on Friday against Baylor will be telling on his availability going forward. However, there was one offensive lineman ruled out for Friday: Tyler Gibson . It is set to be his third consecutive missed game. After making his 2026 debut on Saturday against BYU, Duane Thomas Jr. is now designated as probable for Friday's matchup against Baylor. The senior caught three passes for 16 yards and rushed twice for seven yards; a limited return to be sure. However, wide receivers coach Sean Beckton did say to 96.9 The Game on Oct. 21 that if coaches thought he could play more, he would. Plus, the Knights do not necessarily have to rush him back to a central role, given the target shares Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes and Waden Charles have accumulated. Meanwhile, after missing two games, sophomore Caleb Rollerson now has an opening to return to the field on Friday after being ruled questionable on Tuesday. Despite optimism from Frost on Monday about him being "really close," Lewis Carter has been ruled out for a fifth consecutive game. Jennings was also listed in Tuesday's report, designated as probable . However, it is still going to keep Swint out for at least one more week, which provides another opportunity for Landen Chambers to earn more carries out of the backfield, which he took advantage of against BYU. A trio of EDGEs was all designated probable: Sincere Edwards , Ken Talley and Bruno Dall . Baylor ruled out five of its players in its initial report. Defensive tackle Devonte Tezino started out the season as the Bears' starter, but an injury has kept him out of action since week three. Meanwhile, there are two Bears players designated as questionable : running back Dawson Pendergrass and cornerback Devon Jordan.

home.headline: UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game
home.blurb: Coach Scott Frost said running back Taevion Swint will be back quickly, and linebacker Lewis Carter could be a game-time decision this week . He added that if the senior isn't available against the Baylor Bears, he'll likely be a game-time decision next Saturday against the Kansas Jayhawks . Carter has missed every conference game this season. He went into the medical tent for a knee injury at the end of Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers and was ruled out early for the next game. More Videos The UCF Knights made program history in upsetting the then-No. 2 BYU Cougars , and a few key players are on the cusp of returning for Friday's Space Game. Swint's injury occurred in practice, and Frost said he started limping after a "nothing play." The redshirt freshman missed his first game of the season , leaving room for Landen Chambers to step up in his absence. UCF has relied on the speedster to make plays in the run game and on special teams. Swint's rushed for 162 yards and two touchdowns on 32 carries, and returned seven kickoffs for 209 yards. He scored his first touchdown in the season opener against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats, and the second in the Big 12 home opener against the TCU Horned Frogs . The Knights have missed their defensive quarterback, especially in highly contested losses against the then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys . The senior had a career season last year after transferring from Oklahoma . Carter led the team with 92 tackles and set career highs in tackles for loss, sacks, and fumbles. He became a star at UCF. While at Oklahoma, he was a reserve linebacker and special teams player. Wisconsin transfer Tackett Curtis, the team's leading tackler, has stepped up in Carter's absence. Curtis has 42 tackles (18 solo, 24 assisted), one sack, one fumble recovery, one pass deflection and two interceptions. The Knights are getting healthy at the right time. They aim to build on an upset win and collect two more wins to break a two-year bowl drought. Friday's game against Baylor is one of the more interesting weekday matchups . The program fired coach David Aranda, and Joe Klanderman is the interim coach. UCF's eight-game Space Game winning streak ended in heartbreaking fashion as Houston caught the game-winning interception against former Knights quarterback Davi Belfort. home.headline: UCF Injury Report Raises Concerns Ahead of Top-10 Showdown With BYU
home.blurb: The Knights listed 10 players, including starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III and freshman running back Taevion Swing (162 yards), as questionable or worse on Thursday. Another six players – 4 defense, 1 offense, 1 special teams – are probable for the week's top-10 home test vs. No. 2 BYU, which is hot off its nationally-regarded win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame in Provo. It'll be up to Jenkins, who left the game for UCF in the third quarter of the Houston loss , to test BYU through the air on Saturday with Barnett unavailable, and it'll come as the senior backup grows comfortable as his team's signal caller. The Scott Frost staff displays trust in Jenkins, but the payout hasn't come in the win column following two Big 12 losses at Oklahoma State and Houston; Both losses saw Jenkins combine for 518 passing yards, 5 touchdowns and two interceptions on 53 attempts. To stay within such a low spread, UCF needs a big day out of Jenkins and the offense to keep pace with a BYU squad intent on keeping its perfect 3-0 Big 12 record intact. It's hard to bet against the Cougars, but this home return for UCF after a week off certainly factors into the math as Frost and company look for a big one this weekend when the league's frontrunners come to town. home.blurb: One of the more-promising listings is starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III , who was listed as questionable. Defensive tackle RJ Jackson Jr. and defensive back DJ Bell are both listed as doubtful, adding another level of difficulty to defensive coordinator Alex Grinch's efforts. On Wednesday, UCF released the most-recent injury report, with 16 Knights dealing with ailments. This is extremely-promising signs for UCF's offensive outlook, as he would add a big element to the Knights' passing game ahead of their showdown with No. 2 BYU . Despite initial reports confirming Barnett will not make the start on Saturday, fffensive coordinator Steve Cooper spoke to the media on Tuesday, saying that he thinks there is a fair chance Barnett could see action. Head coach Scott Frost gave promising remarks as well, adding that Barnett is making "really good progress" in his recovery. With the Cougars' offense clicking at a high level, getting Barnett back would help the Knights keep up with the top squad in the conference. On defense, UCF will still be without star linebacker Lewis Carter , who has continued to miss time after a strong early start to his senior campaign. Carter showed the ability to produce against some of the top competition in the conference last season, posting big showings towards the end of the year. In three of the final four games of the season, Carter recorded 12 or more tackles, doing so against Texas Tech , Houston, and the looming BYU Cougars. BYU's run game is one of the offense's biggest strengths, which will be difficult to slow down without Carter in the middle. Last season against BYU, UCF got off to a hot start, and it began to look like the Knights could upset the Cougars and potentially earn a bowl bid. This time around, Frost is hoping to get off to a hot start and maintain it throughout the game - something that the Knights have not been able to do against Oklahoma State and Houston in the past weeks.
